author: Brenton Kemp
title: Hunter Greene (elbow) will began rehab assignment June 18
desc: Reds right-hander Hunter Greene (elbow) is scheduled to begin a rehab assignment in Arizona on June 18.
impact: Greene has been on the 60-day injured list since undergoing surgery on March 11 to remove bone chips from his right elbow. He will now embark on what is likely to be a lengthy rehab assignment, which should consist of at least four or five starts. The hope is Greene will return in July before the All-Star break, but he has some boxes to check before that can take place.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Brandon Lockridge (knee) receives PRP injection
desc: Brewers outfielder Brandon Lockridge (knee) received a PRP injection on Thursday.
impact: Lockridge is back in Milwaukee, undergoing running tests with the team. Once cleared by the medical staff, he will embark on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Nashville. The 29-year-old was hitting .294 with five stolen bases in 28 games before hitting the shelf on May 9.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Andres Gimenez (wrist) scratched from lineup Sunday
desc: Blue Jays shortstop Andres Gimenez has been scratched from Sunday's lineup due to left wrist soreness.
impact: Gimenez was originally slated to play shortstop and hit eighth against Yankees right-hander Will Warren on Sunday, but Ben McAdoo will enter the lineup to play first base with Ernie Clement sliding over to shortstop. Gimenez is slashing .222/.269/.351 with six homers and seven stolen bases through 68 games this season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Eric Sabrowski (elbow) to begin rehab assignment Sunday
desc: Guardians left-hander Erik Sabrowski (elbow) will begin a minor league rehab assignment with High-A Lake County on Sunday.
impact: Sabrowski threw successful bullpen sessions on June 8 and June 11 and will begin a rehab assignment in the low minors on Sunday. The southpaw has appeared in 25 games for the Guardians this season, working to a stout 1.71 ERA after tossing a 1.84 ERA across 33 appearances a season ago.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: George Valera designated for assignment
desc: The Guardians have designated outfielder George Valera for assignment.
impact: Valera will lose his roster spot after the Guardians activated infielder Gabriel Arias (hamstring) from the 60-day injured list. The 25-year-old slashed .216/.237/.297 without a homer or a stolen base across 38 plate appearances in the big leagues this season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Gabriel Arias (hamstring) activated from IL
desc: The Guardians have activated infielder Gabriel Arias (hamstring) from the 60-day injured list.
impact: Arias began a rehab assignment on June 4, and will return to the big leagues on the same day the Guardians placed superstar Jose Ramirez (hand) on the 10-day IL. Arias has appeared in just 10 games for the Guardians this season after hitting .220 with 11 homers and eight stolen bases across 129 contests a year ago.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jose Ramirez (hand) officially placed on IL
desc: The Guardians have placed third baseman Jose Ramirez (hand) on the 10-day injured list.
impact: Ramirez left Saturday's win over the Tigers with a left hamate bone injury, one that will likely cost him four to six weeks on the IL. The best-case scenario for his return would be mid-July, although a return closer to the end of the month is more likelky.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Hunter Brown (shoulder) to officially return Tuesday versus Tigers
desc: Astros right-hander Hunter Brown (shoulder) will make his return to the Astros' rotation on Tuesday at home against the Tigers.
impact: Brown has been sidelined since early April with a Grade 2 shoulder strain, but has looked excellent in his rehab starts and will make his next start at Daikin Park in Houston on Tuesday. Brown allowed just one earned run in 10 2/3 innings spanning two starts before hitting the shelf, a continuance from his breakout 2025 season, in which he posted a 2.43 ERA in 31 starts en route to a runner-up finish in the AL Cy Young voting.

author: Chase Davis
title: Bobby Witt Jr. racks up extra-base hits, but Royals fall short
desc: Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 in a loss to the Astros with two doubles and one run scored.
impact: After Saturday's loss to Houston, Witt is hitting .284 with nine home runs, 28 RBI, 35 runs scored and 24 stolen bases across 71 games. He hasn't hit a home run in 16 games, but he's got a 17% strikeout rate and eight stolen bases in that timeframe.

author: Chase Davis
title: Carter Jensen drives in three as Royals come up short
desc: Carter Jensen went 2-for-5 in a loss to the Astros with two doubles, one run scored and three RBI.
impact: After Saturday's loss, Jensen is batting .220 with eight home runs, 35 RBI, 29 runs scored, and a .298 wOBA across 65 games. Since his move to leadoff at the end of May, he's scored nine runs and picked up 12 RBI in 13 games.

author: Chase Davis
title: Lane Thomas pops homer in tight loss
desc: Lane Thomas went 1-for-3 in a loss to the Astros with a home run, a walk, two runs scored and one RBI.
impact: After Saturday's loss, Thomas is batting .229 with three home runs, 16 RBI, 14 runs scored and three stolen bases across 56 games. He has seen more playing time recently, starting five of his team's last seven games. Vinnie Pasquantino was placed on the IL on Sunday, possibly opening the door for more playing time.

author: Chase Davis
title: Alex Lange takes second consecutive loss
desc: Alex Lange took the loss Saturday against the Astros after allowing one earned run on one hit and one walk while striking out one batter over 1.2 innings.
impact: After the defeat, Lange now has a 4.13 ERA and 1.44 WHIP with a 9.6 K/9, 4 saves and 1 hold through 30 appearances. This makes back-to-back outings with a home run allowed, and the Royals are running out of options. John Schreiber, Daniel Lynch and Matt Strahm pitched earlier in the game, with Lynch being the only one with a scoreless outing.

author: Chase Davis
title: Noah Cameron gets tagged early in tight loss to Astros
desc: Noah Cameron allowed four earned runs on seven hits and no walks while striking out one over 4.1 innings in Saturday's loss to the Astros.
impact: After the defeat, Cameron now has a 4.11 ERA and 1.21 WHIP with a 3-4 record through 13 starts. He came into this game with a 1.80 ERA and 0.67 WHIP over his last five starts spanning 30 innings. He didn't have it in this one as he gave up five hard hits and picked up eight whiffs on 86 pitches. He'll look for better results next time out against the Cardinals at home.

author: Chase Davis
title: Blaze Jordan crushes a big extra-base day vs. Twins
desc: Blaze Jordan went 2-for-4 in a win over the Twins with a home run, a triple, two runs scored and three RBI.
impact: Through two games, Jordan has picked up four hits, two runs and four RBI with an average exit velocity of 99.3 mph. He's started every game since being called up at third base, and with Nolan Gorman sent down, he should see plenty of action at the hot corner.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Rhett Lowder solid in no-decision versus D-backs Saturday
desc: Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder allowed just one earned run in 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision on Saturday against the D-backs.
impact: Lowder certainly pitched well enough to win on Saturday, coming just one out shy of hurling a quality start. He scattered five hits and walked two while punching out six on the evening. He departed with the game tied at one, and the Reds would win this one 2-1 on the back of a Noelvi Marte solo homer in the eighth inning. It was a nice bounce-back effort for Lowder, who lasted just three innings while walking five in his return from the injured list last Sunday. The 24-year-old will carry a 4.60 ERA into his next scheduled start, which will be a tough road matchup against the Yankees next weekend.
